key_insight: Fermion-to-qubit encodings can be viewed as geometric objects, where hypergraph structure and coupling-space transport reveal physically meaningful changes in encoded Hamiltonians beyond spectral equivalence.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers new diagnostics for choosing and analyzing encodings such as BK and XBK when mapping many-body models to qubit hardware.
method: Built weighted hypergraph representations for BK-encoded Hamiltonians.
Defined a geometric observable comparing kinetic vs interaction connectivity in the BK hypergraphs and derived its dependence on interaction strength.
Used coupling-space probability measures and optimal transport to track Hamiltonian reorganization in the XBK representation.
evidence_signal: The framework was tested on Hubbard, spinless tV, single impurity Anderson, and Kitaev models, showing consistent geometric signatures across distinct many-body systems.
watch_item: The framework is encoding-specific and mathematically structural, so practical benefit may depend on how well these geometric measures correlate with simulation cost or hardware performance in real workflows.
paper_title: A Geometric Theory of Fermion-to-Qubit Encodings
